questions.question: A community awareness program visits local high schools to emphasize the dangers of drinking and driving, hoping no crash ever happens. What type of prevention is this?

questions.explanation: Correctly installed seats act before a crash, preventing the injury from occurring.
questions.question: Firefighters set up a free child car-seat check and install seats correctly for parents before anyone leaves the parking lot. What type of prevention is this?

questions.explanation: Giving out helmets and smoke alarms targets hazards early so injuries and fires are kept from occurring at all.
questions.question: A city gives away bicycle helmets and smoke alarms at a health fair and teaches families how to use them. What type of prevention is this?

choices: National EMS Scope of Practice Model
questions.explanation: The model is the national reference for dividing skills among EMR, EMT, AEMT, and paramedic.

Emergency Medical Treatment and Labor Act

questions.explanation: The medical director is checking care on an individual call, which is quality control rather than a system-wide review.
questions.question: The medical director personally reviews one EMT's patient care report from last night's call to check that the required care standard was met. What is this single-call oversight called?

questions.explanation: Direct medical director oversight of the standard of care given on one call is quality control.
questions.question: After a chest-pain call, the medical director calls the crew in to discuss why a protocol step was missed on that specific run. What process is this?

questions.explanation: Call-by-call oversight by the medical director is quality control, unlike CQI's system-wide review.
questions.question: Instead of auditing a year of system-wide data, a medical director spot-checks charts from this week's calls to confirm EMTs met care standards on each call. What is this called?

questions.explanation: Cardiac monitoring is an advanced skill assigned to the paramedic level.
questions.question: On a chest-pain call, one provider places the patient on a cardiac monitor and starts interpreting the rhythm. Which provider level performs this advanced function?

questions.explanation: Endotracheal intubation and emergency pharmacology are paramedic-level advanced skills.
questions.question: A patient needs endotracheal intubation and emergency drugs in the field, beyond basic airway and medication help. Which provider level is trained for this?

questions.explanation: Pharmacologic interventions and advanced treatment skills are functions of the paramedic.
questions.question: A crew requests the provider who can give pharmacologic interventions and perform other advanced assessment and treatment skills at the scene. Which provider level should respond?
